one_month_reasoning: Window is 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08. (1) Q3 2026 results: not yet announced as of Oct 11 (no notice found on IR or EDGAR). Last year the notice came Oct 15 and results Nov 5 after the close (src 18), so a print inside the window is likely (~85%) but unconfirmed. I dropped the round-1 'Nov 4' date because it came from a key-gated feed. Q2 beat consensus by ~17% on EPS ($2.78, src 2) and the stock nearly doubled from April to early September (src 19), so the setup is two-sided: the Sep 16 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% (src 7) is a small tailwind to the ~$105M client-fund interest guide that assumed rates hold (src 2, 5), and September mid-size hiring was firm (ADP 50-499 establishments +54K, src 11; Paychex small-business jobs index steady at 99.15, src 10). Against that, the stock sits above the average ($220) and median ($210) Street targets, BofA initiated at Sell on Sep 29 (src 4), and the FY26 guide implies H2 revenue growth of only ~6%, so a guide that is merely reiterated could disappoint. (2) FOMC Oct 27-28: Polymarket prices no change at 83.5% (src 17, context only); roughly neutral for the stock. (3) ADP's October employment report is due Nov 4 (src 11). (4) Founder 10b5-1 selling cannot begin before Dec 1, 2026, so it is outside the window (src 6). Net: median ~$233 (spot +0.3%), lognormal sigma 15% for the month, above the 46%/3.5 = 13.1% base because of the likely earnings print; lower than round 1's 16% since the print date is no longer treated as certain.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E + 40% DCF, valued at Oct 2027. P/E: NTM EPS $15.02 (0.25 x FY27 consensus $13.97 + 0.75 x FY28E $15.37) x 17.0x (core HCM peer median 17.09x) = $255. DCF: normalized 2026 FCF $575M (guide >$650M less a $74.8M one-off tax inflow) + $31.5M after-tax interest, grown 7.44% to 2027 and less $68M SBC = $584M; 7/6/5/4.5/4% growth, 9.0% WACC (CAPM 8.3% + 0.7pt), 3% terminal, $702M net debt, 42.8M horizon shares = $243. Blend 0.6 x 255.3 + 0.4 x 243.0 = $250.4, rounded to $250.

bear.story: The FY27 guide (Feb 2027) shows recurring growth sliding toward ~5%. The enlarged sales force ramps slowly (management flagged ramp time, src 5), AI-driven seat compression at clients bites, and the BofA bear case wins out (src 4). NTM EPS stalls near $13.5 (below the $13.97 FY27 consensus) and the stock de-rates to the lowest core peer multiple, INTU's 12.64x (src 27): 13.5 x 12.64 = $170.6, about $170. The SMB employment data (src 10, 11) make a recession-driven version of this less likely in the near term, so I do not raise the probability above 25%.

base.story: Revenue grows ~7.4% (FY27 consensus, src 4), the ~46% adj. EBITDA margin holds (src 2), and normalized FCF of ~$575-600M a year goes to dividends and buybacks. NTM EPS of ~$15.0 by Oct 2027 at the 17.0x core peer median (= $255), in line with my P/E method.

bull.story: The new reps ramp, recurring growth re-accelerates to ~10%, margins step up further on automation, and rates stay at or above the post-September 3.75-4.00% range (src 7), lifting client-fund interest above the $105M guide. NTM EPS ~$16.0 at 20.0x (between PCTY 17.61x and NSP 20.94x, below ADP's 22.09x) = $320. Not supported by unverified LinkedIn data any more; the bull case rests on reported Q2 momentum (recurring +11.0%, src 2).

reasoning: Round 2 rebuild after the supervisor review. I re-checked each correction at its source before using it. The 10-Q (src 1) confirms 45,071,619 shares at Jul 28 including 786,338 restricted shares, $198.0M cash, $900.0M debt, H1 OCF $427.6M with a $74.8M income-tax inflow, capex $54.9M, SBC $31.6M and Q2 interest $10.5M. The 8-K (src 2) confirms the Q2 numbers and the FY26 guide. StockAnalysis (src 3, 4) confirms FY27 EPS $13.97, beta 0.83 and targets. FRED (src 8) confirms 5.22% and Damodaran (src 9) 4.20%. The Fed release (src 7) confirms the Sep 16 hike and the 13D/A (src 6) confirms the founder plan. I re-opened PCTY and NSP (src 22, 25) and both matched. I could not confirm the $1,655.5M buyback-authorization figure in the parts of the 10-Q I could read, so no number depends on it; my buyback share count is funded only by FCF. Changes: (a) shares 44.3M -> 45.07M base and 41.5M -> 42.8M at the horizon; (b) FCF base normalized to $575M (and FY28 EPS growth cut from 11% to 10% so I don't double-count the share shrink); (c) discount rate rebuilt by CAPM (8.3%, +0.7pt judgment = 9.0%) in place of a forum narrative; (d) peer median on the core HCM set is 17.09x, so my unchanged 17.0x is at the median; (e) all key-gated Alpha Vantage inputs (consensus, report date) removed; (f) AltIndex LinkedIn data, app ranks and Polymarket odds are context only and no longer support the margin view or bull case; (g) the bear multiple is now the lowest core peer (12.64x) instead of a forum 14.1x. Where I differ from the supervisor: I keep 17.0x rather than 16.75x because PAYC's revenue growth matches PCTY (17.6x) and beats PAYX/ADP, so a discount to the median is no better argued than a premium. I use the verified 0.83 beta plus an explicit 0.7pt judgment add rather than a 0.95 beta. Result: P/E $255, DCF $243, blend $250 (from $261). New in-lane evidence: the Paychex Small Business Employment Watch (src 10) and ADP's September report (src 11), both checkable at the publisher. They show stable small-business and firm mid-size (50-499) hiring, which supports keeping consensus revenue growth in the base case and holding bear odds at 25%. Scenarios: $170/$255/$320 at 25/52/23%, a mean of $249. Ladder: a 90/10 mixture of lognormal(median $236, sigma 0.37) and a fat left tail (median $200, sigma 0.60). Overall median ~$233 and mean ~$251, consistent with the $250 fair value and the scenario mean. I keep sigma below the 46% realized volatility because that figure includes the 2026 crash-and-recovery; the tail term restores downside for leverage, AI and guide risk. P(>= $232) = 0.507, down from 0.55. Lane accounting: 8 of 29 sources are in-lane (28%). The required peer comps take 10 aggregator pages and basic facts must come from filings; excluding the comps, 8 of 19 (42%). Sources 10, 11 and 15-17 are ones other lanes are unlikely to use. Research limits: the Paycom prepared-remarks PDF was not text-readable in this environment, the IR news page did not render, and sec.gov refused a script download, so filings were read through WebFetch.
